checks: The convex lower graph 3|z|−3 and affine upper bound give a compact convex body with interior. Its base projection is exactly [−1,1], and the only integer fibers are [0,1], [−3,1], [0,1].

For the closed cap x≤0 its strict complement in each fiber is (0,1], giving unit uncaptured length on each and relative remainders (1,1/4,1). At threshold one half the selected endpoints omit their integer midpoint.

The unit cube padding preserves the three positive fibers, multiplies the numerator and denominator by the same unit volume, and leaves a nonzero continuous normal. af89470c3209e9d8:07 §6 contains this precise example and padding.

overlap.comparison: That different three-fiber example combines several relative capture conditions with concave absolute remainder roots and fails to cover the source. It does not give failure of lattice convexity for one fixed relative-remainder threshold.
The accepted residual program uses absolute local residual roots and affine majorants. The example here keeps absolute remainder constant and varies its relative fraction.

readability: The strict remainder is measured after removing the entire closed cap, including its boundary. This changes no lengths here, and makes the threshold convention explicit.

summary: The exact three-fiber construction and continuous product padding refute lattice convexity of the half-remainder superlevel set in every indicated dimension.
